subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should Telegram/ACP source turns enforce core action-claim verification or fail-closed diagnostics when visible final text claims completed file, message, or external side effects without matching tool or audit evidence?
rationale: Current main has delivery-mode policy, private-final warnings, PostToolUse-style hook plumbing, and QA honesty scenarios, but no generic runtime invariant; choosing one changes privacy, compatibility, delivery, plugin-policy, and provider-runtime behavior.

options.title: Define Core Verification Policy
options.body: Specify which side effects require evidence, how missing evidence is diagnosed or suppressed, and which source-reply privacy invariants must be preserved before implementation.

options.title: Limit Core To Stranded-Final Recovery
options.body: Treat #85714 as the bounded core fix and leave broad action-claim checks to later design work, hooks, or plugins.

options.title: Document Current Limitation
options.body: Keep current source-reply semantics, document that arbitrary action-claim verification is not enforced, and route detection to PostToolUse/audit hooks or ClawHub plugins.

recommendation.title: Define Core Verification Policy
recommendation.body: Specify which side effects require evidence, how missing evidence is diagnosed or suppressed, and which source-reply privacy invariants must be preserved before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history on source-reply policy, ACP dispatch, and audit/hook surfaces that frame the decision.
